title: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
lede: On Nvidia's first earnings call since Jensen Huang resigned, interim CEO Colette Kress said the company still backs open models and still intends to buy Hugging Face.

points: Kress pointed to OpenRouter's weekly token volume, up 35-fold in a year and 3.5-fold in three months, as a sign open models speed adoption.
The $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal, agreed in September, would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia's history.
Hugging Face serves more than 18 million developers and 200,000 companies; analysts did not ask about the deal in the Q&A.
Kress called Nemotron, the open-weight family Huang pushed for agentic and reasoning work, the most used US open model on OpenRouter.
Huang's exit had raised doubts about the strategy he championed; Hugging Face's CEO vowed to keep fighting for open-source AI.

sections.text: Hugging Face hosts much of the open-weight ecosystem and Nemotron is a common base for agent work, so builders on open models get a signal that neither is being reconsidered for now.
